newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goodman sees smaller future abnormals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goodman sees smaller future abnormals.

text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Thursday it would post abnormal losses in future years as it continues rationalising and restructuring, but that they would be smaller than the A$72.2 million of abnormal losses posted in 1995/96.
"We will have abnormals, but I think they'll be smaller and of a higher quality nature than those we've had," Goodman chief executive David Hearn told a news conference.
"Probably, it's not the end," Hearn said of the abnormal losses.
He said future abnormal charges would be related to investments in the future like rationalisations, rather than reflections of past losses and writedowns.
Earlier Goodmans reported a group net profit of A$28.3 million for the year to June 30 compared with a loss of A$52.8 million a year earlier.
Goodman's pre-abnormals net profit rose 3.5 percent to A$100.7 million, in line with analysts expectations of around A$100 million.
Goodman's shares were unchanged at A$1.30 at 1.15 p.m. (0315 GMT).
